09a_1_kinetic_weights.png: The sizes of the weights $1/f_\mu$ with which a derivative along each direction enters the energy-momentum tensor, on a logarithmic vertical axis (pure numbers). Left: along the history $b_4 = e^{4a_4/3}$ (in the unit $b_4(0)$), against $a_4$ from $-2$ to $2$ at $z = \pi/4$; the 3-space weight $e^{-a_4}$ falls, while the extra-time weight $e^{a_4}b_4^{-1/2}(\sin^2 z)^{-1/12}$ and the hidden weight $e^{a_4}b_4^{-1/2}|\tan z|$ both rise like $e^{a_4/3}$, because the block of the hidden direction and the extra times deflates; the time weight is $1$. Right: against $z$ from $0.02$ to $\pi - 0.02$ at $a_4 = 0.5$, $b_4 = e^{2/3}$; the hidden weight grows without bound at the fold $z = \pi/2$ (gray line), where the two halves of the cell meet, and the 3-space weight does not depend on $z$.

09a_3_diagonal_parts.png: The eight diagonal entries $T^\mu{}_\mu$ (right bar of each group) of the random configuration of the previous figure, each split into its kinetic part, the sum of the kinetic terms $K_\nu$ of the other seven directions (left bar), and its potential part $-(mS + U)$ (middle bar), in units of energy per unit volume. The potential part is the same in every direction; the entry at $x_4$ is $-\rho$, and the others are the pressures $p_0$, $p_3$ (three of them) and $p_t$ (three).
09a_4_volumes_first_law.png: The 3-space volume $V_3 = e^{3a_4}$ (solid), the extra-time volume $V_t = e^{-3a_4}b_4^{3/2}(\sin^2 z)^{1/4}$ (dashed), the hidden length $V_0 = e^{-a_4}b_4^{1/2}|\cot z|$ (dash-dotted) and the 7-volume $V_7 = \sqrt{|g|} = e^{-a_4}b_4^2|\cot z|(\sin^2 z)^{1/4}$ (dotted) of a coordinate box at fixed $x_0$, along the deflating history $a_4 = AHx_4$, $b_4 = e^{4AHx_4/3}$ with $A = 1$, $H = 0.25$, for $x_4$ from $0$ to $8$, each divided by its value at $x_4 = 0$; logarithmic vertical axis. $V_3$ grows like $e^{3AHx_4}$, $V_t$ shrinks like $e^{-AHx_4}$, $V_0$ like $e^{-AHx_4/3}$, and $V_7$ grows like $e^{5AHx_4/3}$. Read as a first law, the conservation identity says: while 3-space inflates a positive $p_3$ takes energy out of the box, while the block deflates positive $p_t$ and $p_0$ put energy in, and the growing 7-volume dilutes the energy density.
09a_5_hidden_balance.png: The hidden-direction pressure profiles $p_0 = P + c\,(\sin^2 z)^{-1/4}$ that satisfy the conservation identity along $x_0$, $\partial_0 p_0 = -3H\cot z\,(p_0 - p_t)$, when $p_t = P = 1$ is constant, for $c = -0.4, -0.2, 0, 0.2, 0.4$; horizontal axis $z = 6Hx_0$ from $0.1$ to $\pi - 0.1$, across the fold $z = \pi/2$ (gray line) into the second half of the cell, vertical axis $p_0$ in units of energy per unit volume. Only $c = 0$ (solid line) is independent of $x_0$, and it has $p_0 = p_t$; every other profile is flat at the fold, where $\cot z = 0$, and grows in size like $|\sin z|^{-1/2}$ towards $z = 0$ and $z = \pi$, where the extra times degenerate.
